title: Keep each agent session's state and expose it as cdx agents --json

needs: A dashboard or another tool (a hub, a terminal board, a chat agent) can ask cdx which sessions are working, waiting for their user, done or stopped by a usage limit, without parsing transcripts or terminals.
context: cdx notify already receives every Claude Code and Codex hook event with the cdx session name, but only turns it into a desktop or tray notification and keeps nothing.
Consumers seen so far: a web hub across several machines, a chat agent driving cdx through MCP, terminal boards built on cdx.
cdx run --failover cannot be combined with --detach, so background runs started detached never fail over on a usage limit.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Every hook event cdx notify receives updates one small state record per cdx session (session, provider, cwd/project, state working|waiting|done|failed|limit, reason, last prompt head within the existing privacy rules, updated_at), written atomically under the cdx home, even when desktop alerts are muted or off.
AC2: The hook needed for state is provisioned for every session that opts in (a setting distinct from desktop alerts, or notify on), for Claude Code and Codex.

AC3: cdx agents [--json] lists the records, waiting first, drops records older than a configurable age, and marks a session whose process is gone as ended; nothing in it can change a hook decision (stdout stays silent in the hook path).
AC4: A limit stop is recorded as state limit with the account's reset time when known, using the same two-signal rule as run_failover so a guess never marks a healthy session.
AC5: --failover works with --detach: the detached supervisor applies the failover decision, and the run registry records the move.
AC6: Tests cover state transitions, muted alerts still recording, stale and ended sessions, the silent-stdout rule and detached failover; README/docs updated.

product.title: Agent state in cdx
product.overview: cdx already sees every agent event through its hook; keep the latest state per session and expose it so other tools can orchestrate without scraping.
goals: One cheap, local answer to: which session needs me, which is busy, which hit a limit.
Detached background runs survive a usage limit like attached ones.
non_goals: A dashboard or UI in cdx itself beyond the CLI listing.
Shipping state between machines: consumers fetch cdx agents --json where they need it.

backlog_items.title: Failover for detached runs
backlog_items.priority: Medium - unattended runs die on a usage limit
problem: --failover needs a watching process, which --detach gives up, so detached runs never move to another account.
scope_in: Failover decision applied by the detached supervisor, registry entry for the move, tests.
acceptance_criteria: AC5: --failover works with --detach: the detached supervisor applies the failover decision, and the run registry records the move.
AC6: Tests cover state transitions, muted alerts still recording, stale and ended sessions, the silent-stdout rule and detached failover; README/docs updated.
